title: Structure padding, alignment and object representation
learningObjectives: Explain the concept and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify data or resource flow.
Recognize relevant safety and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested C program.

understand.concept: Implementations may insert padding between structure members and at the end of a structure to satisfy alignment requirements. sizeof(struct) includes such padding. The byte representation of a structure is not automatically a portable file or network format.
understand.whyItMatters: Assuming a fixed structure layout can break binary compatibility across compilers, architectures and build options. Portable serialization should encode fields explicitly.
understand.analogy: Treat each object or stream as a resource with a defined lifetime and explicit rules for access.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal object, storage-duration, alignment or library rules.

explain.narrative:
Implementations may insert padding between structure members and at the end of a structure to satisfy alignment requirements. sizeof(struct) includes such padding. The byte representation of a structure is not automatically a portable file or network format.

Check all allocation, I/O and conversion results. Respect object bounds and lifetime, initialize data before reading it, and define who owns and releases each resource.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: offsetof is declared in stddef.h, which should be included for this example. The offset and total size depend on the implementation's layout and alignment rules.

practise.guidedTask: Predict why sizeof(struct Record) may exceed sizeof(char) + sizeof(int).
practise.independentTask: Inspect sizeof and offsetof for several structures on your compiler and explain why the results are not universal.
hints: Use offsetof from stddef.h rather than guessing member offsets.
Padding bytes may contain unspecified values; do not compare structures with memcmp as a general equality test.
Serialize fields with a defined byte order and format rather than writing raw structure bytes for portable interchange.
